title: On-chain investing, explained for fund & ETF investors
disclaimer: Educational content only, not financial or investment advice. On-chain assets can be volatile and you can lose money.

slides.title: You can see your fund's **statement**. Not your fund.
slides.subtitle: A 2-minute intro to on-chain investing, in plain English.

slides.title: There's a lot of plumbing between you and your money.
slides.body: A fund house, a custodian, a registrar, a broker. Each one does a real job. But each adds **time**, a **cost**, and a layer you don't see.

left.label: Traditional
items: Trades settle in a day or more
Your record sits in their database

right.label: On-chain
items: Your record on a public ledger

slides.title: A public ledger anyone can check.
slides.body: Every buy, sell and rebalance is recorded on a shared ledger. It leaves a **receipt** that can't be quietly edited later.

slides.title: Why it matters to you
items: **Ownership:** assets sit in an account only you control
**Speed:** move money in minutes, not days

slides.kicker: A familiar idea on new rails
slides.title: Index investing, rebuilt in the open.
slides.body: Like an index fund, an on-chain portfolio can follow a basket and **rebalance automatically**. The difference: you can watch every rebalance happen.

slides.title: New rails, new risks.
slides.body: On-chain markets are younger and can swing harder. Technology has its own risks. So learn first, start small, and never invest money you can't afford to lose.

slides.title: Learn it before you need it.
slides.body: One plain-English idea a week on how investing is changing. No hype, no jargon.
